answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock a fixed bond for 30 days before it can receive a daily job quota. The same rule applies to agents mapping tundra routes, managing a grove, or scheduling harbor freight. Creating more names therefore earns no free capacity: an attacker running 1,000 identities must fund 1,000 bonds and keep that capital unavailable for a month. The defense makes fake identities costly without pretending to prove they are unique people.
